evidence: Read the full diff of fe93ba4 and dense() in internal/memory/search.go lines 292-373 at the head.

No-chunk memories: best[i] is copied from first[i] and only a matching chunk row updates it, so the score is first + 0.15*(first-first), bit-identical to the old dot(qv, v). Filtered-out chunk rows and rows with a mismatched dimension are skipped as before.
Score bound: best >= first, so the score is a convex combination of first and best; it never exceeds the old plain maximum (so never above cosine 1) and never falls below first.
Confidence: search.go:190 reads dense[0].Score, still a cosine-scale value; a late chunk lifts a score by at most 0.15*(best-first).
Hybrid fusion (search.go:488-491) and the widen path consume dense() output, so they inherit the identical no-chunk score.

Tests: TestLateChunkDoesNotOvertakeABetterFirstWindow pins cosine 1/sqrt2 for the short memory and 0 for a non-matching long one; TestDenseLiftsAMemoryByItsBestChunk pins the lifted formula and ConfidenceLow. Hybrid and widen share the same score code path.
